chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Wasshash from Aban from Amr ibn Khalid from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Gabriel (peace be upon him) said: O Messenger of Allah, we do not enter a house that contains an image of a human, nor a house in which one urinates, nor a house that contains a dog.
ai.seo_question: What are the three conditions that prevent angels from entering a house according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the angelic protocol of purity, linking physical cleanliness (urination, dogs) with spiritual decorum (human images). In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes the principle that spaces for prayer must be free from both ritual impurities and distractions that hinder divine presence, reflecting the holistic view of *taharah*.
